title: Flattening by an admissible blowup (Raynaud--Gruson)
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme which is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], let $U\subseteq T$ be a quasi-compact open subscheme, and let $g:W\to T$ be a morphism of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] which is quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism] and whose restriction $g^{-1}(U)\to U$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Then there is a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ of finite type with $\mathcal I|_U=\mathcal O_U$ (a $U$-admissible blowup centre [def-nagata-admissible-blowup]) such that, writing $\pi:T'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(T)\to T$ for its blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup], the strict transform $W'\subseteq W\times_TT'$ of $W$ [def-nagata-strict-transform], namely the scheme-theoretic closure in $W\times_TT'$ [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image] of the open subscheme lying over $T\setminus V(\mathcal I)$, is flat over $T'$ and of finite presentation over $T'$, that is, locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
